Build a circular layout

Source: R/circos-layout.R
circos_layout.Rd

A circos_layout turns a set of nodes and links into polar coordinates. Everything a plot needs is computed once, here, and returned as data: the arc of every node, the sector each node belongs to, and the angular slot reserved for every link endpoint. Layers never recompute any of it.

Usage

circos_layout(
  x,
  nodes = NULL,
  sectors = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  gap = 0.01,
  sector_gap = 0.05,
  start = 0,
  slot_fill = 0.9,
  slot_gap = NULL,
  self_loops = FALSE,
  loop_depth = 0.5,
  tracks = NULL,
  track_offset = 0.06,
  radius = 1,
  weight = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'circos_layout'
circos_layout(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'matrix'
circos_layout(x, nodes = NULL, ..., columns = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
circos_layout(x, nodes = NULL, ..., columns = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_graph'
circos_layout(x, nodes = NULL, ..., columns = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'igraph'
circos_layout(x, nodes = NULL, ..., columns = NULL)

Arguments

x

A square matrix, a data.frame with from/to columns, a tidygraph/igraph object, or an existing circos_layout.

nodes

An optional node table. Needs an id column; label, sector and any further columns are carried through to the layers.

sectors

Sector assignment: either the name of a column of nodes, or a named character vector mapping node ids to sectors. Nodes are grouped in the order given (first appearance, or the order of the vector's names).

order

Node order around the circle: NULL keeps the input order, "hclust" clusters nodes by link strength, a character vector gives an explicit order, and a function is called with the node table and must return node ids.

gap

Fraction of a full turn left as a gap between neighbouring nodes.

sector_gap

Extra fraction of a turn left between sectors.

start

Angle (radians) of the first node arc.

slot_fill

Fraction of a node's arc that its link slots occupy (slots are centred inside the arc).

slot_gap

Absolute seam in radians between adjacent link slots on a node, the way circlize::chordDiagram()'s diffHeight is a fixed height. NULL (the default) keeps the seam at the 1 - slot_fill fraction, which shrinks with the node's arc; a fixed value keeps the ribbons visibly separate on a wide ring with many links.

self_loops

Draw self-links (from == to) as small loops folded toward the centre (spec sec.4.7). FALSE (the default) drops them with a message.

loop_depth

How far a self-loop folds toward the centre, as a fraction of the node's radius at most: the depth is loop_depth * slot_span / node_width of the radius, so a narrow node gets a shallow loop. In (0, 1]. Ignored when self_loops = FALSE.

tracks

Named numeric vector of outer track widths, e.g. c(values = 0.2, heat = 0.1). Widths are relative to the unit node ring.

track_offset

Gap between the node ring, and between tracks. The first track band starts at 1 + track_offset, so keep it at or above the node ring's outer edge (0.05 with the default geom_node_arc()).

radius

Base radius of the node ring. 0 puts the ring on the spine of a linear (coord_arc()) layout.

weight

Name of the column holding each link's weight, e.g. weight = "r". When set, the geometry follows the values: a node's arc is proportional to the weight it carries and a slot is proportional to its link's weight (negative values count by magnitude). NULL, the default, gives every node an equal arc and every link an equal share of it – the value then only shows through aes(fill = ).

by

Name of a node-table column to lay out one ring per group of its values (spec sec.9.1). Returns a circos_layouts list, each element a full layout with a panel attribute; a link belongs to the group named in its own column of the same name, or – without one – to the group of its two ends (a link spanning groups is dropped). NULL builds one layout.

...

Used by the methods to build the node table from graph objects.

columns

Optional named character vector mapping the layout's column names onto your data's, e.g. c(from = "qaccver", to = "saccver") for BLAST table output. The rename is a copy; columns you do not map travel with the link table, so weight = and aes() can still reach them.

Value

An object of class circos_layout, or – when by is given – a circos_layouts list of them.

See also

ggcircos(), layout_nodes(), layout_links()

Examples

m <- cor(mtcars)
l <- circos_layout(m, order = "hclust", tracks = c(values = 0.2))
head(layout_nodes(l))
#>     id label sector order n_links    theta0    theta1     theta     width r
#> 1 carb  carb    all     1      10 0.0000000 0.5083668 0.2541834 0.5083668 1
#> 2   wt    wt    all     2      10 0.5711987 1.0795655 0.8253821 0.5083668 1
#> 3   hp    hp    all     3      10 1.1423973 1.6507641 1.3965807 0.5083668 1
#> 4  cyl   cyl    all     4      10 1.7135960 2.2219628 1.9677794 0.5083668 1
#> 5 disp  disp    all     5      10 2.2847947 2.7931615 2.5389781 0.5083668 1
#> 6 qsec  qsec    all     6      10 2.8559933 3.3643601 3.1101767 0.5083668 1
head(layout_links(l))
#>   from   to          r self_loop .circos_w .circos_from_arc .circos_to_arc
#> 1  mpg  cyl -0.8521620     FALSE         1                8              4
#> 2  mpg disp -0.8475514     FALSE         1                8              5
#> 3  cyl disp  0.9020329     FALSE         1                4              5
#> 4  mpg   hp -0.7761684     FALSE         1                8              3
#> 5  cyl   hp  0.8324475     FALSE         1                4              3
#> 6 disp   hp  0.7909486     FALSE         1                5              3
#>   edge_id   theta0   theta1    theta theta_end0 theta_end1 theta_end x        y
#> 1       1 4.153443 4.199196 4.176319   1.739014   2.196544  1.967779 1 4.176319
#> 2       2 4.204279 4.250032 4.227156   2.551687   2.780452  2.666070 1 4.227156
#> 3       3 1.885876 1.936713 1.911294   2.297504   2.526269  2.411886 1 1.911294
#> 4       4 4.102606 4.148359 4.125482   1.489781   1.642291  1.566036 1 4.125482
#> 5       5 1.829391 1.880227 1.854809   1.150870   1.303380  1.227125 1 1.854809
#> 6       6 2.415064 2.472255 2.443659   1.320326   1.472836  1.396581 1 2.443659
#>   xend     yend .circos_node_width .circos_loop_depth
#> 1    1 1.967779          0.5083668                0.5

layout_tracks(l)
#>    track width   r0   r1
